title: White Chocolate Mocha
source: Copycat of the Starbucks White Chocolate Mocha (grande: 2 shots, steamed milk, white chocolate)

items.body: Run hot water through the steam wand into the mug to warm it, then pour the water out. Put the white chips in the empty mug.
Pull the double shot straight onto the chips in the mug. Let it sit 30 s, then stir until the chips melt and the espresso is smooth, ≈1 min. Lumps left? Microwave the mug 10 s and stir again.

Pour the cold milk into the steaming pitcher (no more than ⅓ full). Purge the wand, sink the tip just under the surface and steam, letting in a little air for the first 5 s for a thin layer of foam. Then lower the tip and heat to 150 °F (66 °C), when the pitcher is too hot to hold, ≈30–45 s.
Wipe and purge the wand. Tap the pitcher on the counter and swirl to break big bubbles. Pour the milk into the mug, holding back the foam with a spoon, then spoon the foam on top.
Drizzle the caramel sauce over the foam in a crisscross. Serve right away.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: Branded Foods labels (Meijer Vanilla White Baking Chips, 11 oz, FDC 2632879; Ghirardelli Premium Caramel Sauce, 16 oz, FDC 2580730) and SR Legacy (espresso 171891; whole milk 171265). Whipped cream not counted.
notes: Starbucks’s white mocha has no caramel; skip the drizzle for the classic drink (412 kcal). For a caramel white mocha all the way through, stir the caramel into the espresso with the chips instead.
Sweetness: 3 tbsp chips is café-sweet. Use 2 tbsp (30 g) for less sweet. The Meijer chips are “vanilla white” (palm oil, no cocoa butter), so they melt thinner than real white chocolate. Stir well.
Starbucks tops it with whipped cream: a short pull from the iSi Gourmet Whip works, not counted above.
Iced: melt the chips in the hot espresso, stir in the cold milk unsteamed, then pour over a cup of ice.
